purpose: The structured record of the Stage 0 gate: the pre-flight that runs before the first clone and whose failures halt the run rather than get repaired. Every entry below is a verification whose failure stops the run, never a step whose failure is repaired. Nothing was installed, upgraded, substituted or provisioned, and neither artifact tree was created or cleared by this run.
provenance: Every value in this file was produced by running the command recorded beside it on this host and capturing its output verbatim. No value is inferred, none is a placeholder, and none is copied from a prior run without its provenance being named. Where a figure was read from a provisioned evidence file rather than re-measured at this gate, the file is named in the entry's observed_source field. Where a value could not be established it is recorded as inconclusive with what was tried, never upgraded to a pass.

governing_rules.substitute_standard: Enterprise best practice held to the AAP's own four principles, restated here because they are what this file is judged against:

principles.name: Verification is independent of the thing verified
principles.applied_here: The heap check is the load-bearing example. The host is shown to COMMIT the heap, not merely to have the memory: java -Xms64g -Xmx64g -XX:+AlwaysPreTouch -version exiting zero is the test, and it is strictly stronger than reservation. /proc/meminfo is NOT that test and appears in this file only as context, in check gate.host_capacity_context, explicitly labelled as not the test.
principles.other_instances: The nine argument guards were established by reading the scripts rather than by probing them, because a blind probe against a defective runner could perform a real scan and contaminate the artifact tree. The harness/bin classification was enumerated independently rather than taken from the environment record.

principles.name: Reject rather than infer
principles.applied_here: A check whose outcome could not be established is recorded as inconclusive with what was tried. No check in this file carries a verdict that was not produced by the command recorded beside it. Where a rule count was read from a provisioned evidence file rather than re-measured, the entry names the file and says so rather than presenting it as this gate's own measurement.

principles.name: Halt-and-report over silent repair
principles.applied_here: Nothing here is installed, upgraded, substituted or provisioned. Every item is a verification. The two artifact trees are neither created nor cleared by this run. No runner file and no baked flag was edited. Each check carries halt_condition_if_failed naming the AAP 0.9.2 condition that would have stopped the run, so a reader can see that the alternative to a pass was a halt and never a remedy.

principles.name: Verbatim preservation
principles.applied_here: Every command's stdout and stderr is carried as it was emitted, including the empty string where a stream was empty and including output a tool wrote to stderr rather than stdout. Nothing is summarised in a stdout field.

governing_rules.never_fabricate: A gate record is the proof behind every downstream claim about the environment. An invented version string, or a pass recorded for a check that was not run, destroys the value of every document that cites it. Nothing in this file was invented.

write_ordering.constraint: AAP 0.6.1 and 0.9.1 require this file to be written only after the emptiness check on both artifact trees has passed, so that it cannot be the thing that makes harness/artifacts/logs/ non-empty.
write_ordering.relationship: emptiness_check_timestamp_utc (2026-08-24T17:01:36.594Z) STRICTLY PRECEDES this_file_written_at_utc (2026-08-24T17:06:49.246Z) by 312.652 seconds. The check was taken first, its result was held in memory, and this file was composed afterwards from that held result. This file therefore cannot be the thing that made harness/artifacts/logs/ non-empty.
write_ordering.emptiness_rule_scope: The emptiness rule covers harness/artifacts/raw/ and harness/artifacts/logs/ ONLY. A provisioned sibling under harness/artifacts/ would not violate it and is never cleared; the AAP cites harness/artifacts/smoke/versions.txt as exactly such a sibling in an earlier provisioning. This provisioning has no such sibling: ls -A harness/artifacts returned exactly 'logs' and 'raw'.
write_ordering.divergence_between_the_two_trees_after_t: By AAP design the two trees diverge from Stage 1 onward. harness/artifacts/raw/ stays runner-only — exactly one artifact per tool that writes one, and nothing else ever. harness/artifacts/logs/ legitimately accumulates this run's own evidence, of which this file and runner-metadata.json are the first two entries.

authority_rule.statement: The request's expected-values table governs every field it carries, and the harness's own environment record never overrides it. Four cases exhaust the possibilities and this file is where they are adjudicated.

cases.both_state_and_differ: The table governs, and that row's rule applies. Instances in this file: the datadog SAST ruleset digest, the two Trivy database timestamps and the Dependency-Check NVD timestamp. Each is recorded with BOTH values, each takes verdict recorded_difference, and each additionally marks that tool's counts not comparable with the rehearsal.
cases.table_states_and_record_silent: The table governs and the silence is noted. No instance arose at this gate: every anchor the AAP table carries is also carried by harness/ENVIRONMENT.md.
cases.record_states_table_silent_observation_a: Both are recorded, the field is marked unanchored, and the run continues. Instances are listed in unanchored_fields below.
cases.record_states_table_silent_observation_c: Both values are recorded and the run HALTS, because there is no anchor to adjudicate between them and continuing would mean choosing one silently. No instance arose at this gate; halts is empty.

authority_rule.boundary_that_matters: This rule reaches INHERITED facts only — what this run observes about the provisioning as it found it, read before this run changes anything. It does NOT apply to outputs this run deliberately replaces. If the environment record carries the previous graph's size, digest or counts, a graph this run builds will differ, and that difference is the request being fulfilled rather than an environment contradiction. Reading intentional replacement as a contradiction would halt the run for succeeding. Every entry where the distinction could be misread carries a classification field of 'inherited' or 'deliberately_replaced', and the deliberately_replaced set is enumerated separately below.

verdict_vocabulary.note: Closed set. Every checks[].verdict below is one of these four literals.
verdict_vocabulary.pass: The observed value satisfies the expectation. The run proceeds.
verdict_vocabulary.recorded_difference: The observed value differs from the expectation. BOTH values are recorded and the run proceeds, per AAP 0.9.3. Where the difference is a ruleset digest or a feed timestamp, that tool's counts are additionally marked not comparable with the rehearsal, because a different rule set produces a different count for reasons that have nothing to do with the code.
verdict_vocabulary.halt: The observed value triggers a condition in AAP 0.9.2. The run stops and reports; the condition is never repaired. Every halt entry names the 0.9.2 condition it falls under.
verdict_vocabulary.inconclusive: The check's outcome could not be established. What was tried is recorded. Never upgraded to a pass.

Three inherited ruleset or feed identities differ from the AAP's expected values; each is recorded with both values and marks its tool not comparable with the rehearsal, which AAP 0.9.3 places explicitly in the record-and-continue class. No value was inconclusive, so nothing downstream has to work around an unestablished fact.
